title: Canonical ordinary maps in the finite proper external product
statement:
Use the finite coefficient datum $k,A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $B,Y,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $a:Y\to B$, $b:Z\to B$ proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Put $C=Y\times_BZ$, with projections $r:C\to Y$, $t:C\to Z$ and $c=ar=bt$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Work in ordinary unbounded constant-$A$ derived categories on the small pro-etale sites, with the pullback, tensor and signed symmetry of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For arbitrary $H\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $J\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ write $F=Ra_*H$, $G=Rb_*J$, $E=Lr^*H\otimes_A^LLt^*J$. Let $x=\operatorname{Ex}_{*,a,b,H}:Lb^*F\to Rt_*Lr^*H$ and $\pi_u$ be exactly the ordinary counit-defined exchange and projection maps of [def-exchange-projection]. Define
$$\begin{aligned}
v&=\pi_{t,Lr^*H,J}\circ(x\otimes1_J):Lb^*F\otimes_A^LJ\longrightarrow Rt_*E,\\
w&=Rb_*(\sigma_{J,Lb^*F})\circ\pi_{b,J,F}\circ\sigma_{F,G}:F\otimes_A^LG\longrightarrow Rb_*(Lb^*F\otimes_A^LJ),\\
\Omega_{a,b}(H,J)&=\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}\circ Rb_*(v)\circ w:F\otimes_A^LG\longrightarrow Rc_*E,
\end{aligned}$$
where $\kappa_{b,t}:Rc_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rb_*Rt_*$ is the canonical finite-level compositor of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. Use the canonical pullback tensor and composition comparisons [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso, lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] and the ordinary derived adjunctions $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$. Write $\varepsilon_{u,K}:Lu^*Ru_*K\to K$ for their counits.  The operations and displayed maps are constructions only, without any asserted identities. Also write pairEvaluation(e,d) for the tensor of arbitrary evaluation arrows e:P_a F→H and d:P_b G→J after the same pullback tensor and composition comparisons; swapStructure is the projection equality s;c′=c and swapPull is its pullback comparison. The same equality comparison is also presented objectwise by objectwiseComparison; its naturality is equality elimination followed by naturality of the given comparison. swapPull uses this presentation to expose its object components without expanding the concrete functors.
